tagline.text: The City of Golden Friendship, where laughter breaks out on the rapids

location.label: Location
location.text: Cagayan de Oro City, Misamis Oriental

children.text: The hub city of northern Mindanao, famous for white-water rafting on the Cagayan de Oro River that cuts through downtown. It's the gateway to Camiguin, Bukidnon, and Iligan, and still has caves, canyons, a giant Christ statue, and a weekend night market — plenty to fill a day or two of city sightseeing mixed with adventure.

Cagayan de Oro (often shortened to CDO) is the administrative and commercial center of northern Mindanao and, with a population of over 700,000, the region's second-largest city. True to its nickname, "the City of Golden Friendship," people here are known for their warmth, and the name "de Oro" ("of gold") is said to come from tales of gold panned from this river in Spanish times. The Cagayan de Oro River runs through the heart of the city, with the Bukidnon plateau rising like a screen behind it.

What made this city famous across the Philippines is white-water rafting. Water flowing down from the Bukidnon plateau forms large and small rapids as it passes through a canyon on the city's outskirts, and several operators run courses where even first-timers can ride the rapids safely with a guide. This has earned CDO the nickname "the Adventure Capital of the Philippines," and activities like canyon trekking, canyoneering, and ziplining are all clustered within
1 hour
of the city.
Historically, the city was also the site of the Battle of Macahambus Hill in

, where Filipino forces defeated American troops during the Philippine–American War. Downtown holds older landmarks like the San Agustin Metropolitan Cathedral, Gaston Park, and Xavier University's Museo de Oro, alongside big shopping malls such as Limketkai, Centrio, and SM, so it's easy to find whatever you need while traveling.

CDO is a transport hub for Camiguin Island, the Bukidnon plateau (Dahilayan and the Del Monte pineapple plantation), and the waterfalls around Iligan. Most travelers spend a day or two here enjoying rafting and city sightseeing before heading to their next stop. It suits young travelers who love activities, anyone circling northern Mindanao, and residents looking for a short getaway during a business trip.

blocks.title: White-water rafting on the Cagayan de Oro River

children.text: The beginner course covers about 14 rapids over roughly
3 hours
and can be joined even if you can't swim. Experienced rafters might try the advanced course (
4–6 hours
), which takes on 20 or more rapids.
A limestone cave and deep gorge about
30 minutes
from downtown by car. This is where Filipino forces defeated American troops in
, and a short trail runs through the cave to a viewpoint over the gorge.
A statue of the Divine Mercy Christ, about

tall, standing on a hill in El Salvador City to the west, with sweeping views over Macajalar Bay. It's a leading pilgrimage site for Filipino Catholics and gets especially crowded on weekends and during Holy Week.

A forest park on the city's eastern outskirts, popular for canyoneering — following a valley downstream and leaping into waterfalls along the way. Horseback riding and light trekking are also available.

blocks.title: Gaston Park and San Agustin Cathedral

children.text: The Spanish-era plaza of Gaston Park and the cathedral beside it are at the heart of CDO's history. Watching locals stroll and snack around the plaza at sunset gives a good feel for the city's everyday atmosphere.

blocks.title: Weekend night market and street food

children.text: On Friday and Saturday nights, a night market fills the Divisoria street area with stalls selling barbecue, grilled seafood, and fresh fruit shakes. With live music playing, it's a good window into the local youth nightlife.

An archaeology and folklore museum inside Xavier University, exhibiting the indigenous cultures and prehistoric artifacts of northern Mindanao. It's small, but a good way to understand the region's history.
A dish combining charcoal-grilled pork (sinugba) and vinegar-cured raw fish (kinilaw), common at restaurants across northern Mindanao. Pairing it with cold beer is the local way to enjoy it.
Get picked up by your rafting operator, head upriver, and enjoy the beginner or advanced rafting course.

CDO sits on Mindanao's northern coast, so it's less exposed to direct typhoon strikes but still gets rain year-round. From
February
to
May
, when rainfall is comparatively lower, is the best time to visit. From
June
to
October
, afternoon showers are frequent, and from
November
to
January
, the northeast monsoon and low-pressure systems bring heavier rain on some days.

Rafting runs year-round, but the course varies with the river's water level. In the dry season the current is a bit gentler, which suits beginners, while in the wet season higher water makes the rapids more thrilling — though operations may pause right after heavy rain for safety. Having experienced major flooding from Typhoon Washi in
, it's wise to avoid riverside activities when heavy rain is forecast.
The city's signature festival is the Kagay-an Festival in
August
, held around the feast day of the city's patron, St. Augustine (
August 28
), with street parades and performances. Accommodation prices rise during this period and around Christmas, so book ahead.

Accommodation is most convenient around Limketkai Center and Centrio Mall (the uptown area near C.M. Recto Street). It's close to malls and restaurants, and the airport shuttle van also picks up and drops off nearby. Business hotels run about
a night, international chain hotels about
, and budget inns and pensions about
. For a quieter stay, resorts in the Uptown area or the coastal Opol district are also an option.

CDO's food combines northern Mindanao seafood with produce from the highlands. Besides sinugbang lauya, popular dishes include sinigang with fish head, grilled tuna jaw over charcoal, and roast pig (lechon). Binaki, a steamed corn cake made from Bukidnon corn, is a signature snack of both CDO and Bukidnon, and Del Monte pineapples from the plantation are cheap and sweet too. In the evenings, grabbing something light at the barbecue stalls along the coastal promenade, near the malls, or at the weekend night market is a favorite pastime for locals. There are also a few Korean restaurants downtown, so long-term residents have little trouble finding familiar food.
Rafting trips mostly depart in the morning, so it's best to book with an operator by the evening before. Check whether the price includes accommodation pickup, helmet and life vest, and a guide.
For rafting, wear clothes you don't mind getting wet and strapped sandals or water shoes. It's safer to put your phone in a waterproof pouch or use the operator's photo service.
The Laguindingan Airport shuttle van departs in line with flight arrival times, so it's best to head straight to the boarding counter as soon as you collect your luggage.
Bus terminals are split by direction — remember that Camiguin and Butuan-bound buses use Agora, while Iligan-bound buses use Bulua.
ATMs are plentiful around the malls and downtown, making cash withdrawals easy. Rafting sites and outlying attractions like Macahambus, however, take cash only.
The Divine Mercy Shrine has a dress code, so sleeveless tops or very short shorts may not be allowed inside.
The night market mainly runs on Friday and Saturday nights, so it's worth including one of those evenings in your schedule.
Right after heavy rain, the river level can rise sharply. If the operator suspends the trip, it's safer to reschedule rather than push ahead.
During rafting, follow your guide's instructions and keep your feet forward in a seated position. If you're thrown from the boat in a rapid, this posture matters most for avoiding rocks.
Watch out for phone and wallet pickpocketing in crowded spots around the night market and malls.
Travel advisories are in effect for parts of Mindanao. Check your home country's latest travel advisory before you go, and plan your route mainly along main roads.
Low-lying roads can flood during the wet season, so leave plenty of time for getting to the airport.

Always use an operator registered with the city government and a properly certified guide for white-water rafting. Choosing an unregistered operator on price alone can mean inadequate safety gear and rescue systems.
